Theme

Work & responsibility · Money, work & business

fire verb

dismiss from a job

also sack, get the sack, be fired, dismiss, lay off

classical

Suet. Aug. 24.2: cum ignōminiā tōtam dīmīsit
Traupman 305: dismiss, dīmittō
Traupman 305

dīmittō, dīmittere, dīmīsī, dīmissum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

dismiss, let go, discharge

Other words

  • āmoveō, āmovēre, āmōvī, āmōtum — remove (from a post)

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 315: fire (dismiss), āmoveō; Traupman 315 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Classically to remove, take away (Lewis & Short).

  • exauctōrō, exauctōrāre, exauctōrāvī, exauctōrātum — discharge from service; cashier

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Suet. Aug. 24.2: exauctōrāvit; M-O s.v. hire: fire, dismiss · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Of soldiers, discharged with honour or in disgrace (Liv., Suet., Lewis & Short).

  • missum facere — let go, discharge

    also used · classical · Suet. Caes. 69: missam facere legiōnem (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • decimam legiōnem contumācius pārentem cum ignōminiā tōtam dīmīsit, item aliās immodestē missiōnem postulantēs citrā commoda ēmeritōrum praemiōrum exauctōrāvit

    the tenth legion, which obeyed with insolence, he dismissed in disgrace to a man, and others who demanded their discharge rudely he discharged without the rewards due for completed serviceSuet. Aug. 24.2

See also employee, job, manager, let go.
